article_briefs.brief: Tata Motors raised its all‑cash voluntary tender offer for Iveco to 14.40 euro per share, up from 14.10 euro per share, which would value the transaction at 3.91 billion euro if all 271.2 million Iveco common shares are tendered. The acceptance period runs from September 7 to October 26, 2026, with Iveco Group shareholders scheduled to vote on related resolutions at an extraordinary general meeting on October 16. Tata Motors said the price increase reflects a slight delay in the completion of the offer due to longer‑than‑expected authorisations, and the revised price represents a 33.47 per cent premium over Iveco's share price on July 17, 2025 and a 6.77 per cent premium over the price on July 29, 2025. The additional payout will be funded through an 85 million euro credit facility agreement with MUFG Bank Ltd, GIFT Branch, and Tata Motors noted that the revised offer will not be increased further.

Tata Motors has lodged its “best and final” €3.91‑billion offer for Iveco Group at €14.40 a share, ruling out any higher bid. A shareholder vote this week could lower the acceptance threshold from 95 per cent to 80 per cent, with Exor committing its 27.06 per cent stake and controlling more than 43 per cent of voting rights, while minority investors such as Davidson Kempner, Syquant Capital and Petrus Advisers are estimated to hold about 20 per cent. The offer, up‑priced from €14.10 to €14.40 a share adding about €81 million, must be tendered by investors before the October 26 closing, and if completed would create a global commercial‑vehicle group with roughly €21 billion in annual revenue and annual sales of around 5,90,000 vehicles.

Stellantis India, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd (TMPV) and its subsidiary Tata Passenger Electric Mobility Ltd (TPEM) signed a Definitive Agreement on Monday to broaden their partnership into advanced technology and product collaboration. Under the agreement, TMPV will give Stellantis access to its advanced product technology and vehicle architecture, which Stellantis will apply through its Indian product development and engineering capabilities to serve the requirements of more than 50 global markets. The vehicles will be manufactured in India at Fiat India Automobiles Private Limited (FIAPL), the 50:50 joint venture between TMPV and Stellantis in Pune. The deal builds on the MoU signed in February 2026 and was highlighted by comments from Shailesh Chandra, MD & CEO of TMPV, and Tianshu Xin, COO of Stellantis Asia‑Pacific Region.

Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Stellantis signed a definitive agreement on October 12, 2026 expanding their partnership to include advanced vehicle technology and product development. The deal, which builds on a February 2026 MoU, will focus on developing vehicles in India for more than 50 global markets, with manufacturing at Fiat India Automobiles Private Limited, a 50:50 joint venture between the two companies. Stellantis will gain access to Tata Motors' product technology and vehicle architecture and will leverage its portfolio of 14 automotive brands and global product development expertise for the initiative.

Tata Motors raised its offer for Iveco to €14.40 per share, a 2% increase announced on 9 October, representing a 6.77% premium to Iveco’s 29 July 2025 closing price. The tender has so far attracted acceptances for only 28.4% of the shares, while three large shareholders – Davidson Kempner, Syquant Capital and activist investor Petrus Advisers – together hold about 20.4% of Iveco’s common shares and have not tendered, putting the deal at risk ahead of the 26 October deadline. The all‑cash €3.8 billion acquisition, announced on 30 July 2025 (excluding Iveco’s defence business) and expected to conclude by November, would give Tata Motors a foothold in Europe and Latin America and create a combined annual revenue of about €21 billion.

article_briefs.brief: Tata Motors needs to win over silent shareholders—roughly three in four of those who stayed away from Friday’s special shareholder meeting—to reach the 80% acceptance required to complete its €3.9 billion acquisition and delist of Iveco. Shareholders holding about 52.9% of Iveco’s common shares, including promoter Exor with 27%, backed the deal, but about 27% of common shares owned by non‑voting investors must still be persuaded, and opposition remains with 37.27 million votes (≈13.7% of 271.2 million) cast against Chandrasekaran’s appointment versus 211.93 million in favour, plus 34.05 million against Balaji and 35.61 million against Wagh. Tata Motors sweetened the offer by 2% from €14.10 per share to €14.40 on 9 October, and a Tata executive said the current Iveco share price trades below the offer, making it fair, while noting that if the 66.67% threshold is met but not 80%, the acquisition could proceed without full control, complicating delisting and restructuring plans.

Tata Motors CV is expected to post Q2FY27 revenue growth of roughly 44‑45% YoY, with JM Financial forecasting Rs 24,218.4 crore (up 43.6% YoY and 25.3% QoQ) and Motilal Oswal Financial Services projecting Rs 24,638.1 crore (up 45.4% YoY). The company recorded domestic commercial‑vehicle volume growth of about 43% YoY, with JM Financial estimating 1,35,114 units (up 42.7% YoY and 24.5% QoQ) and MOFSL projecting 1,37,339 units (up 43% YoY and around 26.3% sequentially over 1,08,700 units in Q1FY27), driven by a 53.1% YoY rise in LCVs and a 31% increase in MHCVs. While a net price hike of 2.5% has been in place since July, JM Financial expects EBITDA margins to improve sequentially whereas MOFSL anticipates a sharper decline, and MOFSL retains a Neutral rating with a target price of Rs 422 against a market price of Rs 415 (≈2% upside).

Tata Motors overtook Mahindra & Mahindra to become India’s second‑largest passenger vehicle manufacturer by domestic dispatches in the first half of FY27, with dispatches surging 43% to over 3.9 lakh units during April‑Sept 2026 versus Mahindra’s just under 3.6 lakh units, a growth of around 20%. Mahindra’s combined BE and XEV model dispatches jumped 82% to 42,338 units, raising their share of passenger vehicle volumes from 7.8% a year earlier to 11.8%. Tata’s utility vehicle dispatches rose 59%, while overall domestic passenger vehicle dispatches grew 28.3% to around 26.4 lakh units in the same period.

Iveco Group shareholders at an extraordinary general meeting in Amsterdam approved all resolutions related to Tata Motors’ proposed €3.91 billion acquisition, reducing the minimum share acceptance threshold from 95 per cent to 80 per cent. The approval, which also authorises amendments to Iveco’s Articles of Association, delisting, appointment of new directors and a post‑offer demerger if at least 80 per cent of shares are secured, fulfills several conditions for Tata Motors’ subsidiary TML CV Holdings to declare its voluntary public tender offer unconditional. Tata Motors had raised its offer price on October 9 from €14.10 to €14.40 per share, and the tender offer is scheduled to close on October 26, unless extended, subject to remaining offer conditions.

Iveco shareholders at an extraordinary general meeting in Amsterdam approved all resolutions linked to Tata Motors' voluntary public tender offer, including lowering the minimum acceptance threshold from 95 per cent to 80 per cent of Iveco's common shares. Tata Motors had raised its offer price by EUR 0.30 per share to EUR 14.40 (from an initial EUR 14.10 per share) for an acquisition valued at around EUR 3.8 billion (nearly Rs 38,240 crore), with the earlier offer valuing the transaction at approximately EUR 3.82 billion. The tender offer acceptance period runs from September 7 to October 26, 2026, and the approvals also cover amendments to the articles of association, board appointments, conversion of Iveco into a private limited liability company upon delisting, and conditions for a post‑offer demerger if at least 80 per cent of shares are owned.

Competition in the passenger‑vehicle segment is intensifying, highlighted by Mahindra’s 82% rise in BE and XEV model dispatches and its share of passenger‑vehicle volumes climbing to 11.8%, underscoring the shift toward electric models in the market.

Tata Motors has sweetened the offer by 2% from €14.10 per share to €14.40 on 9 October and says the current Iveco share price is below the offer, but if it only reaches the 66.67% threshold it could complete the acquisition without delisting, leaving minority shareholders and preventing the planned demerger; the combined entity is projected to generate about €21 billion of revenue and sell over 590,000 vehicles annually.

Tata Motors Commercial Vehicles (TMCV) is projected to post Q2FY27 revenue growth of about 44‑45% YoY, with JM Financial forecasting Rs 24,218.4 crore (up 43.6% YoY) and Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL) forecasting Rs 24,638.1 crore (up 45.4% YoY). MOFSL maintains a Neutral rating with a target price of Rs 422 against a market price of Rs 415, implying approximately 2% upside, and analysts flag input‑cost inflation, pricing realisation and vehicle mix as key determinants of the upcoming results.

Three investors – Davidson Kempner, Syquant Capital and Petrus Advisers – built stakes worth a combined €728 million in Iveco between July 2025 and September 2026 and now stand to gain about €63 million at Tata Motors’ revised offer price of €14.40 per share, plus an estimated €288 million in extraordinary dividends received in April. They collectively hold about 20.4% of Iveco’s common shares, and their tender decisions are critical as Tata needs to reach an 80% threshold; as of 21 October shareholders had tendered about 33.4% and the offer closes on 26 October. Petrus values Iveco at about €18 per share, roughly 25% above the offer, while Tata’s acquisition – announced in July 2025 for about €3.8 billion and contingent on the €1.7 billion defence business sale to Leonardo – would create a combined business with annual revenue of about €21 billion and sales of more than 590,000 vehicles.

Swiggy reported a consolidated loss after tax of Rs 922 crore for the September quarter, narrowing from Rs 1,092 crore in the year‑ago period but widening sequentially from Rs 792 crore in the June quarter. The results keep the food‑delivery and quick‑commerce platform in focus as investors track September‑quarter earnings.

On October 23, 2026, Tata Motors Ltd announced its Q2 FY27 consolidated profit rebounded to ₹1,257 crore, with revenue rising 36.3% year‑on‑year. The company reported the results in a regulatory filing, and the profit increase follows a prior quarter decline. Shares fell ahead of the announcement, with the stock down 3.97% to ₹397.80 on the NSE.
